description:
Poll everything that happened: messages, contacts, groups, numbers, quotas.

This is how an agent learns about inbound messages without hosting a
webhook endpoint.

**Events come back newest first, so polling for new ones uses
`ending_before`, not `starting_after`.** Typical loop: call with no
cursor and remember the id of the FIRST event in the page (the newest
one); next time, pass that id as `ending_before` to get only what has
happened since. An empty page means you are caught up.

`starting_after` does the opposite: it walks BACKWARD into history,
which is what you want for reading a backlog, and never what you want
for noticing something new. Passing the last id you handled to
`starting_after` in a loop returns steadily older events and never
reaches the present.

`request_id` returns everything that came of one earlier call. A write
tool's result carries `request_id` when the platform issued one; keep it
and you can ask later what became of that specific send.

`number_id` restricts to one number and keeps matching its events after
the number is renamed. `number_alias` restricts to one inbox by the
alias it had when the event happened, so a rename hides the older
events; the two can be combined. Either one excludes `storage.*` and
`media.unavailable` events, which belong to the organization rather
than to any one number.

Most events carry a `number_alias` telling you which inbox they belong
to, and `number_id` (`num_…`), the same number's permanent identifier.
The alias is the one at the time of the event and can be renamed later;
the `number_id` cannot. You need one of them: message, contact and group
ids are unique but not self-addressing, so an id alone does not tell you
which number's tools to use with it, and both work as `number_alias` in
the other tools. Read the fields defensively rather than assuming they
are there: `storage.*` and `media.unavailable` belong to the
organization as a whole and have no single number to name, so on those
the keys are absent rather than empty.

created_gte.description: Only events created at or after this instant. ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`.
created_gte.title: Created Gte

created_lte.description: Only events created at or before this instant. ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. `2026-09-10T00:00:00Z`.
created_lte.title: Created Lte

ending_before.description: Catch up: return events NEWER than this id. Pass the newest id you have already handled to see only what has happened since. This is the one to poll with.
ending_before.title: Ending Before

event_type.description: Filter to exactly one event type, e.g. `message.received`. Common ones: `message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.read`, `message.received`, `message.reacted`, `message.edited` (a text or caption edit, or a calendar event that was edited or canceled), `message.calendar_responded` (a guest answered a calendar event), `message.quota.warning`, `number.connected`, `number.disconnected`, `contact.created`, `contact.quota.warning`, `group.joined`, `group.participants_added`. Use `event_types` instead to filter on more than one at once.
event_type.title: Event Type

event_types.description: Filter to several event types at once, e.g. `message.sent` and `message.delivered`. Same vocabulary as `event_type`. The API accepts at most 20.
event_types.title: Event Types

limit.description: How many events to return, 1-100. Defaults to 25.
limit.title: Limit

number_alias.description: Restrict results to one inbox by the alias it had when the event happened, so events from before a rename are missed. Use `number_id` to follow a number across renames. **Absent means every number**, which is the usual choice. Note this is a filter, not a subject: unlike the messaging tools it does not default to `main`. Setting it also excludes `storage.*` and `media.unavailable` events, which belong to the organization rather than to any one number.
number_alias.title: Number Alias

number_id.description: Restrict results to one number by its `id` (`num_…`, as returned by `list_numbers`). It keeps matching the number's events after the number is renamed, unlike `number_alias`, which matches the alias the number had when the event happened. Can be combined with `number_alias`. Absent means every number. Setting it excludes `storage.*` and `media.unavailable` events, which belong to the organization rather than to any one number.
number_id.title: Number Id

request_id.description: Return only the events that came of one earlier call (`req_…`). A write tool's result carries `request_id` when the platform issued one; keep it and you can ask later what became of that send.
request_id.title: Request Id

starting_after.description: Read further back: return events OLDER than this id. This is the one for walking a backlog, and the wrong one for noticing something new.
starting_after.title: Starting After

name: list_events
title: Poll the organization's event log
